key_insight: Four lung nodule detection models on routine photon-counting CT showed substantial disagreement, with no clear consensus on which nodules to flag.
clinical_relevance: In real-world CT workflows, this means model choice can strongly affect what gets detected, so local validation is important before deployment.
method: Retrospective study of 1,860 routine PCCT scans from a single center (2021–2024).
Compared four deep-learning nodule detectors: TotalSegmentator, nnDetection, RadYOLO, and a commercial CAD system.
Assessed agreement in 1,699 unannotated scans, sensitivity in 25 manually annotated scans, and false positives in 136 report-negative scans.
evidence_signal: Detected nodules varied widely across models; about 1,300 nodules were found by all four models, while 15.4%–37.4% of detections were unique to a single model, and sensitivity ranged from 0.71 to 0.83.
watch_item: Results came from one center and a small annotated test set, so generalizability and performance in other PCCT settings may differ.
paper_title: Comparing Deep Learning Models for Lung Nodule Detection on Photon-Counting CT Images in a Non-Screening Setting
